entries.clue: One Gentleman of Verona, please, out of costume (9)

blocks.note: an Italian gentleman is a signor
to please is to amuse
SIGNORAMUSE loses its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A character from Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen of Verona begs to be let out of his stage costume.
annotation.walkthrough: This puzzle ran on April Fool's Day, and every 'one' in it is a fool. The Shakespeare play is a red herring: Verona just makes the gentleman Italian.
annotation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant person, one of the puzzle's many kinds of fool.

annotation.definitionFit: Sawney is an old, originally Scottish word for a simpleton.

entries.clue: Wound up, Porky packs fine punch (4)

annotation.surface: A wound-up character called Porky throws a good punch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Porky' looks like a name or a pig; it is British rhyming slang (pork pie = lie). F goes in after FIB's first letter, then the lot is reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain informal synonym: to biff someone is to hit them with your fist.

annotation.definitionFit: Epigaeal describes organisms living or growing on the ground's surface.

entries.clue: Aussie one, not half sweet, embracing Georgia (5)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is often British slang for 'very much'; here it is literal, halving BONBON.
annotation.definitionFit: Bogan is Australian slang for an uncouth, unsophisticated person.

entries.clue: There’s no better one (4)

annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a single boast, but it splits in two: GOAT is Greatest Of All Time, and to act the goat is to play the fool.
annotation.definitionFit: The GOAT has no better; and a silly old goat is a fool.

annotation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish, gullible person.

entries.clue: One tick working a little lower (8)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is not 'further down' but 'one who lows', i.e. moos; a little one of those is a calf.
annotation.definitionFit: A mooncalf is a foolish, absent-minded person.

entries.clue: This time alpha particle appears at intervals (5)

annotation.definitionFit: The puzzle was published in April, so April is 'this time'.

entries.clue: A gross baby, born today in a field? (8)

gr. is the abbreviation for gross

annotation.surface: A mucky newborn baby arrives today, out in a field.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Today' is the puzzle's date, 1 April, which falls under Aries; an Arian is someone born under that sign.
annotation.definitionFit: Agrarian means relating to fields and farming.

entries.clue: Cut Pointless – 21s haven’t got it (4)

annotation.surface: Fools would never get onto the TV quiz Pointless, which has been axed.
annotation.walkthrough: Italicised, Pointless is a British TV quiz show, but it is really just 'no use'. 21 down is FOOL, so 21s are fools.
annotation.definitionFit: Nous is common sense, which fools lack.

entries.clue: It perhaps rather fuzzily aired Bugs Bunny features? (8)

annotation.definitionFit: April Fool comes after April; a fool is also a fruit dessert.
